slides.heading: Array Of Products
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Array Of Products, a medium arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Out[i] = product of every element except a[i], without division.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Out i equals product of every element except a i , without division. Prefix products then suffix products.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Each output is the product of everything to the left times everything to the right, so two sweeps replace division.
slides.narration: Each output is the product of everything to the left times everything to the right, so two sweeps replace division.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: for each i, multiply all others → O(n²)
Total product ÷ a[i] → O(n), but breaks on zeros (and is disallowed)
Prefix × suffix products → O(n), no division
slides.narration: The brute force recomputes a product of n minus one numbers for every index, which is quadratic. Dividing the total product by each element is linear, but it breaks on zeros and the problem forbids it. Prefix and suffix products give linear time without division.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Fill each slot with the running product from the left
2. Sweep from the right with a second running product
slides.narration: Step by step. First, fill each slot with the running product from the left. Second, sweep from the right with a second running product. Third, multiply it in. Fourth, no division needed.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Left pass: out[0] = product of everything left = 1
slides.narration: Left pass, index 0: everything to the left multiplies to 1, so out 0 becomes 1.

slides.narration: Left pass, index 1: everything to the left multiplies to 5, so out 1 becomes 5.

slides.narration: Left pass, index 3: everything to the left multiplies to 20, so out 3 becomes 20.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Right pass: out[3] ×= 1 → 20
slides.narration: Right pass, index 3: everything to the right multiplies to 1, so out 3 becomes 20.

slides.caption: Right pass: out[0] ×= 8 → 8
slides.narration: Right pass, index 0: everything to the right multiplies to 8, so out 0 becomes 8.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: The first loop writes the running product of everything to the left into each slot, then multiplies the running value by a i. The second loop goes right to left with a fresh running product and multiplies it into each slot.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of n output.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Zeros: one zero → only its index is non-zero
slides.narration: Zeros are the classic trap: with one zero, only that position gets a non-zero product; with two, everything is zero. The prefix-suffix method handles both automatically. Watch for overflow with big inputs.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Mention the division idea and why it fails
Follow-up: O(1) extra space (reuse the output array)
slides.narration: Bring up the division idea and explain why it fails. Our version already uses the output array for the prefix pass, so extra space is constant beyond the output.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Each output is the product of everything to the left times everything to the right, so two sweeps replace division.
slides.narration: To recap Array Of Products: Each output is the product of everything to the left times everything to the right, so two sweeps replace division. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
